scenes.heading: Bearings
scenes.say: “Go south-east” is vague. “Head one hundred and twenty-five degrees” is exact. Sailors, pilots and hikers use bearings, and with right-angled triangles you can work out exactly where you end up.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A clock lying on the map with 12 pointing north
scenes.science: A bearing sweeps clockwise from north, from 000° to 360°
scenes.breaks: A clock has 12 hours; bearings use 360 degrees, always measured from north.
scenes.say: Imagine a clock lying flat on the map, with twelve pointing north. A bearing tells you how far to sweep the hand clockwise from twelve. A quarter turn is east, ninety degrees. Halfway is south, one hundred and eighty. Three quarters is west, two hundred and seventy.

scenes.heading: True and compass bearings
scenes.say: First the compass cross. Then a line pointing south-east. Measured clockwise from north, it is one hundred and twenty-five degrees true. Measured from south towards east, it is fifty-five degrees, so its compass bearing is south fifty-five east.
scenes.caption: Clockwise from north: 125°T. From south towards east: 55°, so S55°E.

scenes.heading: Reverse bearings
points: Bearing of B from A: stand at A
scenes.say: The bearing of B from A means you stand at A. To go back the other way, add one hundred and eighty degrees, or subtract it if the bearing is already over one eighty. So zero seventy reversed is two hundred and fifty.

scenes.heading: Bearings make right-angled triangles
scenes.say: A ship sails forty kilometres on zero fifty. Draw the north arrow, then the path. Dashed lines north and east make a right-angled triangle. North is adjacent to fifty degrees: forty cos fifty, about twenty-five point seven one. East is opposite: forty sin fifty, about thirty point six four kilometres.
scenes.caption: North = 40 cos 50° ≈ 25.71 km. East = 40 sin 50° ≈ 30.64 km.

scenes.heading: Two legs at right angles
scenes.question: 12 km on 035°T, then 9 km on 125°T. Distance and bearing from the start?
scenes.say: The two bearings differ by ninety degrees, so there is a right angle. Pythagoras gives fifteen kilometres. Inverse tan of nine twelfths gives about thirty-six point nine degrees from the first leg. Add the first bearing: about zero seventy-two degrees true.

points: Compass: N or S first, then E or W
Add θ to the first bearing
scenes.say: Quick recap. True bearings go clockwise from north, with three figures. Compass bearings start at north or south. Reverse a bearing by adding or subtracting one eighty. Draw a north arrow at every point, and remember to add the angle back onto the first bearing. Now try the practice questions!
